easy.def: Very, or to a great amount.
examples: I am so happy.
The soup is so hot.
She is so tall.

more.def: To a great degree, or very much.
examples: The night sky was so clear that we could see thousands of stars.
I was so tired after the hike that I fell asleep in the car.
Thank you so much for the lovely gift.

easy.def: A word that tells what happened because of something.
examples: It rained, so we stayed in.
I was hungry, so I ate.
He is sick, so he is home.

more.def: A word used to show that something happened as a result of what was just said.
examples: The bridge was closed, so we took a different road.
I forgot my lunch, so my friend shared hers with me.
The batteries were dead, so the toy stopped moving.

easy.def: A way to fix a problem.
examples: I found a solution. We can share the toy!
What is the solution to the math problem?
The solution was to ask for help.

more.def: The answer to a problem or the way to fix it.
examples: The solution to the puzzle was hidden in the last clue.
There is no easy solution to the traffic problem.
The class worked together to find a solution.

easy.def: An amount that is not all and not none.
examples: I want some milk.
Some kids are late.
She ate some of the cake.

more.def: An amount or number of something that is not stated exactly, or only part of a group.
examples: Some birds can fly very long distances without stopping.
I need some paper for my drawing.
We saw some deer near the river this morning.

easy.def: A thing that you do not know or name.
examples: I hear something.
She wants something to eat.
He found something shiny.

more.def: A thing that is not named or not known exactly.
examples: There is something under the bed, and I think it is the cat.
I would like to learn something new about space.
She whispered something to her friend.
I am sorry I was late.
She said sorry to me.
He felt sorry.

more.def: Feeling sad or ashamed about something you did, or sad for someone else.
examples: I am sorry that I broke your pencil.
We felt sorry for the lost puppy.
He said he was sorry for being rude.
